name: cli-pipeline-template
purpose: Template for validating a multi-process CLI pipeline before the platform executes several external CLIs through adapters and pipes.

reader_guide.summary: Use this template when one user action should launch multiple CLI processes, connect stdout/stderr/stdin, merge results, or fan out/fan in independent CLI work.
how_to_read: Read execution_policy to confirm shell usage is disabled by default and each CLI is allowlisted.
Read processes to see each process node, adapter, argv command, cwd, timeout, and output bound.
Read pipes to see how streams are connected. Do not hide pipes inside command strings.
Read safety_controls and resource_controls before any implementation that actually starts processes.
Read source_provenance and plan_evidence to see why this process graph is justified.
update_triggers: The platform adds a process runner or local daemon that launches more than one CLI.
Pipe, fan-out, fan-in, cancellation, timeout, output bound, or merge behavior changes.
A desktop shell or web monitor starts invoking local CLI pipelines.
Command execution security, allowlist, secret handling, or resource cleanup rules change.

reference_links.title: Bash Reference Manual: Pipelines
used_for: why shell-style pipes should be modeled explicitly in platform process graphs

reference_links.title: OWASP OS Command Injection Defense Cheat Sheet

structure_rules.rule: Represent pipelines as process nodes and pipe edges instead of putting `|`, `;`, redirects, or chained shell logic inside command strings.
structure_rules.reason: Explicit graphs are easier to validate, inspect, cancel, retry, and explain in history.

structure_rules.rule: Each process uses command plus args arrays. Shell execution requires a separate recorded security review.
structure_rules.reason: Argv-style execution avoids unnecessary shell parsing and reduces injection/portability risk.

structure_rules.rule: Every required process needs cwd, timeout_seconds, max_output_bytes, and cleanup/cancellation policy.
structure_rules.reason: Multi-process orchestration can otherwise hang, leak child processes, or store oversized output.

structure_rules.rule: Only allowlisted adapters may appear in the process graph.
structure_rules.reason: The installable platform must remain CLI-neutral while still controlling which attached capabilities can run.

structure_rules.rule: A multi-process pipeline must name how outputs are merged or released downstream.
structure_rules.reason: Fan-out research and multi-CLI workflows need a deterministic fan-in point before results affect plans or artifacts.

field_guide.meaning: Stable identifier for the planned pipeline.
CLI process nodes. Each node names an adapter, executable command, argv args, cwd, env allowlist, timeout, and output bound.
Explicit stream edges from a process stdout/stderr to another process stdin, file, or artifact.
Global execution constraints such as shell_allowed=false, argv arrays, explicit pipe graph, explicit cwd, and adapter allowlist.
Named controls that must be consciously present before execution.
Timeout, output bound, cancellation, cleanup, orphan-process, and backpressure rules.
Where the process graph and command-execution assumptions came from.
Why this pipeline structure is justified instead of a single command, separate manual steps, or another tool.

purpose: Collect source metadata with one CLI and pass the accepted output to a planning CLI as an explicit pipe.

resource_controls.timeout_policy: Each process has timeout_seconds; timeout cancels downstream execution.
resource_controls.cancellation_policy: Cancel child processes and close stream handles on failure.
resource_controls.cleanup_policy: Wait for child processes, close stdin/stdout/stderr handles, and remove bounded temporary artifacts.
resource_controls.orphan_process_policy: Terminate the process group when the pipeline is cancelled.
resource_controls.backpressure_policy: Use streaming pipes for small output and bounded temp artifacts for large output.

merge_strategy: Only accepted collector output reaches synthesize_plan; final output is a structured planning report.
plan_evidence: The user asked for multiple internal CLI processes connected through pipes.
Existing CLI adapter policy already requires CLI-neutral external command boundaries.
rollback_plan: Disable the pipeline plan and run the two CLI adapters as separate manual commands.
Keep generated outputs out of downstream plans unless the pipeline check is pipeline_ready.
notes: This template validates a process graph; it does not execute arbitrary commands.
